messages.text: okay Noor, you're officially in. welcome to the chaos.
thanks. i've been looking at the CSO. it's huge though. do we take all of it or just a subset?
definitely a subset. 600 concepts seems like a good starting size? anything more and the graph gets noisy.
agreed. i'll filter for the core areas first. how do we handle the broader/narrower relations in that subset? keep them or flatten it?
keep them. we need the hierarchy for the scoring later. broader concepts should have lower weight than specific ones, basically an idf thing.
makes sense. what about the aliases? users are definitely going to type messy strings like 'ml' or 'deep learning' instead of the canonical name.
yeah, that's the hard part. we need a mapping table for common aliases. maybe you can seed it with some obvious ones to start?
i'll start a csv with ~50 common synonyms. should i include abbreviations and plural forms too?
yes to both. the more noise we catch early, the less the model has to guess later.
okay. one more thing: should the ontology be static for now, or do we plan for user-generated concepts?
static for the hackathon. user-generated is a scope nightmare we don't have time for. let's focus on resolving existing strings to our fixed set.
fair. i'll get that subset and the alias list ready by tomorrow then.
perfect. ping me when it's done so i can test the resolution pipeline against it.
